description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) discusses how the conflict in the Middle East is creating "massive economic uncertainty" for her constituents and specifically details how farmers are significantly feeling the impact. Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS), a member of the Senate Agriculture and Budget Committees, defends staying the course in the Iran war, saying the US must “finish the job” to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US, Iran Deadlocked Over Hormuz | Balance of Power: Late Edition 04/22/2026

author: Jeff Mason
description: The bust of John F. Kennedy will remain in the Grand Foyer and the opera house seats will still be red. But officials involved in plans to renovate the Kennedy Center say big changes are coming to the venue.
title: Kennedy Center’s New Chief Makes Case for Two-Year Closure

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: A Virginia judge halted the implementation of a plan to redraw the state’s congressional maps that was approved Tuesday by voters and would have resulted in more US House seats for Democrats.
title: Virginia Judge Blocks Redistricting Plan Approved by Voters

description: Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS), a member of the Senate Agriculture and Budget Committees, defends staying the course in the Iran war, saying the US must “finish the job” to prevent a nuclear-armed Iran even as Strait of Hormuz disruptions push up fuel costs and strain farmers. He also says Congress must pass a reconciliation bill “sooner than later” to keep DHS funded, signaling a vote-a-rama could begin as soon as Wednesday night, and warns he would be “disappointed” by cannabis rescheduling. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Marshall: US Should ‘Finish the Job’ in Iran

description: President Claudia Sheinbaum is considering the head of two local development banks as a candidate for ambassador to the US, a move that would mark the second major personnel shift at the Foreign Ministry ahead of key trade talks, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
title: Mexico Considering Bank Head Lazzeri as Top Diplomat in the US

description: Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) discusses how the conflict in the Middle East is creating "massive economic uncertainty" for her constituents and specifically details how farmers are significantly feeling the impact. description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss stocks sitting near record highs as President Trump extends the Iran ceasefire. Ray Takeyh, Senior Fellow for Middle East Studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, joins to discuss the US and Iran's "new normal" amid the indefinite ceasefire. Then, Bloomberg AI Editor Seth Fiegerman joins to discuss SpaceX saying it has an agreement to acquire AI startup Cursor. Then, Infrastructure Capital Advisors CEO and CIO Jay Hatfield joins to discuss his 2026 market outlook, and why he stands behind his year-end 8,000 S&P 500 price target. Finally, Suburban Propane CEO Michael Stivala on the company's 30th year as a publicly traded company, and customer demand for domestic propane. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Near Record Highs on Iran Truce Extension | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 4/22/2026

description: The US and Iran are locked in a battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz after failing to meet for a fresh round of peace talks even as President Donald Trump says he'll keep a ceasefire in place. title: US, Iran in Battle to Control Strait of Hormuz

description: The one man blocking Donald Trump from installing Kevin Warsh as his new Federal Reserve chair has drawn a red line: the stability of the US financial markets.

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power,  Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the extension of the ceasefire between the US and Iran, a win for Democrats as Virginia voters back their redistricting plan, and reporting that the White House may move to reclassify marijuana. description:
Alex Conant, Partner at Firehouse Strategies and Republican Strategist says that as states finalize new Congressional districts neither party seems to be getting an advantage nationally. 

Virginia voters backed a Democratic plan to redraw the state’s congressional districts in a way that could net them as many as four more US House seats in November’s midterm elections, according to multiple projections. 
With about 99% of the ballots in Tuesday’s referendum counted, the “Yes” vote led the “No” side by 51.5% to 48.6%.  The vote marked one of the final acts in a yearlong national battle sparked when Republicans moved to change voting boundaries in Texas, in an effort to keep GOP control of the US House in the midterms. It also served as an early test for Democratic Governor Abigail Spanberger, who supported the referendum as a response to Republican moves in other states.   (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Neither Party Benefits from Redistricting Fight, Says Strategist Alex Conant
